newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends up, but far off intraday high.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends up, but far off intraday high.

text.p: The won closed higher Monday after rumours spread that the central bank was intervening to slow the won's rapid decline, dealers said.
But dollar buying towards the end of trading brought the won to a close far off the intraday high, they said.
The won ended at 844.60, up from the day's opening rate at 845.50. It ranged from 843.60 to 846.00.
"Rumours that the central bank was determined to keep the won at the 845 level limited dollar buying today," said one dealer. "Many traders hesitated to buy dollars due to the rumours."
The central Bank of Korea, has never officially commented on rumours that it was stepping into the interbank foreign exchange market.
Dealers said the won's downward trend would continue for the time being in line with a slump in exports.
On Tuesday, the won was forecast to trade at around the 845 won level, which dealers saw as the local currency's bottom for this year.
The won's base mid-rate is expected to be set at 844.30 on Tuesday, compared with 844.10 on Monday, dealers said.
